One continuous purposeful action with two beats. 0–3 seconds: medium close shot at anvil height, Hefesto leans into his work and physically closes the sliding caliper jaws on a small copper block held in his other hand. Clear realistic finger articulation; the caliper is a real mechanical tool. As the jaws touch, he lifts his gaze, places the measured block onto the anvil, and turns his shoulders. 3–8 seconds: camera tracks briskly sideways past the anvil edge and arcs 35 degrees, revealing his powerful torso and an immense engraved hydraulic wheel behind him. Hefesto grips a heavy horizontal lever and pulls it toward his body with visible effort. The wheel answers: copper blades begin rotating, dark engraved water surges through their spaces. His robe and curls react to the moving air. The figure stays large in the central half of frame throughout. Anvil edge crossing the foreground provides strong parallax; the wheel is background scale, not a replacement for the character. End while action is alive, with copper motion moving left to right for an editorial match cut.
